title: Chapter 295: Disappearing Arm
html:
The Third Hospital Staff Residence looked old and battered, without even a security booth. Examining the first-floor apartments, Chen Ge realized that none of the doors displayed numbers.

The rental notice only stated Room 304. How am I supposed to find it?

Backpack in hand, Chen Ge waited at the entrance for someone who could give him directions. Ten minutes later, a high school student rode into the compound on an electric bicycle.

“Hello. Could you tell me which building contains Room 304?” Chen Ge called from a respectful distance, careful not to frighten the boy.

“Room 304? That sounds familiar.” The student stopped and gestured deeper into the compound. “It should be somewhere in there, but I’m not sure.”

“One more question, if you don’t mind. Has anything strange ever happened here?” Chen Ge adopted his friendliest expression. “The Electrical Plant Residence is just as old, but it’s far livelier than this place.”

“I don’t think so…” The kid looked at Chen Ge guardedly, thinking that the man was weird.

“Yawen! Who are you talking to?” a middle-aged woman called from the third floor. Chen Ge looked up to find a pajama-clad woman watching him warily and beckoning the student home.

“Coming.” The high-schooler pushed off and quickly left.

“Wait!” Unwilling to lose the opportunity, Chen Ge called up to the woman. He only wanted to collect the drawer, not turn the search into an ordeal. “Ma’am, do you know which building Room 304 is in?”

The moment he finished speaking, every other light in the building went out simultaneously.

“Is it that serious?” Only the middle-aged woman’s home had its lights on.

“Go straight. It’s on the third floor of the first building to your left.” The woman’s expression darkened. She withdrew into her apartment, and its light went out as well.

Why did everyone react like that?Instead of leaving immediately, Chen Ge quietly followed the student. Oblivious to his presence, the boy parked his bicycle and climbed the stairs.

“Mum, what are we having tonight?”

The kid was opening the door when the middle-aged woman could be heard yelling, “Don’t touch the door! Stomp your feet on the ground before coming in!”

“Mum, what are you saying? I just came back from a long study session, and I’m tired.”

“Don’t argue with me!” The woman’s voice rose with startling fury, shocking even Chen Ge where he hid on the second floor. The boy reluctantly obeyed. Only then did she open the door, murmuring, “He’s only a child. He doesn’t understand. Please forgive him…”

She repeated it several times before allowing the kid to enter the room. “Remove your clothes. I’ll wash them for you.”

“But just I changed this morning!”

“No dinner if you don’t change.”

The third-floor door slowly closed. Chen Ge emerged from the stairwell. What is wrong with everyone here?

The drawer’s odds were one in a hundred, compared with Xu Yin’s three in a hundred. Theoretically, the drawer should be somewhat stronger, though still not a Red Specter. Whatever it is, I need to secure it tonight.

Probably because of his earlier shout, very few apartments remained lit. Chen Ge found the building the woman had indicated and sensed nothing unusual upon entering. It looked ancient and partly abandoned. On the third floor stood two adjacent apartments. Neither door bore a number, though a real-estate contact had been pasted on the one to the left.

Is this Room 304?

Chen Ge took out his phone to call the number. It only rang twice before it was picked up. “Thank you for calling Yi Ju Real Estate, how can we help you?”

“I’m interested in an apartment you’re listing at the Third Hospital Staff Residence. I’m already here. Would it be possible to view it tonight?”

“Please wait a minute. I’ll ask our agent who is responsible for that area.”

After a short wait, she returned. “He just finished work, but I explained the situation and he’s heading your way. Here is his number…”

“Thank you.”

About ten minutes later, a friendly-looking man in his thirties arrived outside the building, wearing a black shirt and carrying a briefcase. “What a coincidence—I live nearby. If you wanted to view any other property, you would have had to wait until tomorrow.”

“Sounds like fate if you ask me.” Chen Ge chuckled, thinking about how he could shuttle the drawer away without the man noticing. “How about we go take a look at the room?”

“Of course.” The dark stairwell clearly frightened the man, though he tried not to show it. “Follow me.”

Using his phone as a flashlight, he began his sales pitch. “The neighborhood is quite convenient. There’s a hospital, school, library, and more nearby. And the rent is very affordable.”

On the third floor, the agent produced a ring of keys, each marked with a taped-on number. With his Yin Yang Vision, Chen Ge saw him select the key labeled 305.

“Is this Room 304?” Chen Ge asked.

The keys nearly slipped from the man’s hand. He turned with a brittle laugh. “This is Room 305. Room 304 is haunted, so naturally we wouldn’t…”

“I want Room 304. I don’t mind its history as long as the price is right. Bring me to Room 304,” Chen Ge said firmly. The man gripped the key to Room 304, but he did not dare open the door.

After a long stalemate, the agent approached the other door with a miserable expression. “If I’d known you wanted Room 304, I never would have come.”

He pushed the key into the door. “The price for Room 304 is half of Room 305, but I have to tell you some things just in case you complain to me later.”

“What is it?” Chen Ge focused; he had a feeling that he had won an unusual drawer.

“Room 304’s first tenant was a gambler. He sold everything he owned to repay loan sharks, but it wasn’t enough. Eventually, he jumped from the apartment window and died.”

“That’s the cause of it being haunted?”

“Once I tell you everything, you won’t want the apartment.” The man pushed open the door. “He killed himself after midnight. When the police recovered his body, they discovered that one arm had been severed. It has never been found.”
